macro.text: A reported Khamenei call to end Iran's "neither war nor peace" stance moved markets a little.
Stock futures rise as earnings season continues.
The Fed is expected to hold rates steady this week, but Warsh may point the way to more hikes.
Oil prices seesaw amid renewed diplomatic efforts to end the Mideast conflict.
Tech stocks rally as the AI trade revives.
Nvidia to invest $3 billion in Meta as the two deepen their AI partnership.

read: The tone is risk-on, led by tech: QQQ is up about 1.5% premarket at 714.79 and SPY about 0.9% at 767.05, both above yesterday's closes, while the VIX closed lower near 17.9 and WTI is down about 0.7% near $101 with the 10-year yield flat near 4.99%. There is no high-impact U.S. release today; the only red events are Australian CPI at 8:30 PM ET and the RBNZ rate decision at 9:00 PM ET, both after the U.S. close, so the session is driven by earnings (Boeing, Coca-Cola, UPS before the open) and headlines. The bigger scheduled event is the Fed decision later this week, where a hold is expected but rate-hike guidance from Warsh is the open question. Before taking a setup, it is worth waiting for the first 15-minute range to form and seeing whether QQQ's large premarket gap holds at the open, and keeping an eye on Iran diplomacy headlines, which can move oil and the indexes quickly.
